name: Stats Band
hint: Hover, focus or tap a figure to read how it is counted. Switch the period: the numbers and their pictures morph in place.
description: A landing page's "by the numbers" section where every figure carries its proof. One hero figure leads and the rest stay quiet. Each number counts up once on view, beside a small picture drawn to the chart rules: a sparkline with its spike annotated, a before/after bill bar with the saving hatched, a unit grid where one dot is 10,000 homes, a part-of-whole ring of network regions. Each has a footnoted source. Hovering, focusing or tapping a figure opens a frosted "How we count this" note with the method, the figure and the date range, fitted to the viewport. An optional live counter ticks at a per-second rate that follows the time of day, and only when you pass one. It holds on hover, focus, pause or when scrolled away, then catches up. The period switch (All time / This year) rolls the digits, morphs the line, re-lights the dots and ring and slides the bars rather than re-rendering. Layout follows the section's own width: hero column beside quiet rows when wide, a 2×2 grid at stage width, a single column of rows on phones. Reduced motion shows final values and still pictures. Figures are a <dl> whose accessible text is always the final value. Shows only what you pass: no stats means no figures. Numbers go through your `formatValue` or Intl in `locale`; no currency or unit is assumed. The gallery's sample (an invented energy company) appears only with `demo`.
intents: by the numbers stats section for a landing page
impact metrics band with sources and methodology
animated count up statistics with mini charts
live counter of something happening right now on a marketing page
key figures section with footnotes and how we calculate it
usage: Use once on a marketing page, after the product story, to back it with numbers. Keep it to one hero figure and three or four quiet ones, each with a real source and a one-sentence method; a number you can't explain doesn't belong here. Pass `heading`, `eyebrow`, `lede` and `stats`: each stat is { id, value, label, unit?, unitSpoken?, format? ('integer' | 'percent' | 'compact' | 'currency' with `currency`), decimals?, options? (Intl.NumberFormat options), formatValue?, hero?, visual?, source?, method?, range? }; any field can instead be an object keyed by period id. Pass `periods` ({ value, label, asOf }) for a period switch, controlled with `period` + `onPeriodChange` or seeded with `defaultPeriod`. Pass `liveCounter` ({ label, unit, rate, profile, rateLabel, formatValue, source, method, range }) only if you want a live counter; it never runs otherwise, holds on hover, focus, pause or off screen, and its number is not a live region. `formatValue(value, { stat, period, locale })` formats every figure when Intl options are not enough. Give it the full content width; it picks its composition from its own width. `demo` shows the invented sample (gallery only).
